bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is a subfield of AI focused on systems that learn from data.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial in modern technology, used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Supervised Learning: trained on labeled data to predict known outputs.
Supervised Learning includes Regression (continuous output) and Classification (categorical output).
Unsupervised Learning: trained on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns.
Unsupervised Learning includes Clustering (grouping data) and Dimensionality Reduction (reducing features).
Reinforcement Learning: agent learns by interacting with environment to maximize rewards.
Model Training: feeding data to learn patterns and minimize prediction differences.
Features and Labels: input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: data split for model training and performance evaluation.
Overfitting: model learns training data too well, including noise, leading to poor generalization.
Underfitting: model is too simple and fails to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: models linear relationship for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: predicts probability of belonging to a class for classification.
Decision Trees: non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: inspired by human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: evaluating model performance using separate datasets.
Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score for classification; MSE, R-squared for regression.
Cross-Validation: technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance.
Data Quality and Quantity: need for large, accurate, consistent data; labeling challenges.
Interpretability: difficulty understanding complex models, especially deep learning.
Bias in Data: models inheriting biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: common issues affecting model generalization.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased role in industries due to growing computational power and datasets.
Integration into daily life, enabling smarter technologies across various sectors.
Emphasis on ethical considerations and responsible AI practices as the field progresses.
